quotes.text: And to the sealed house, send the one thin measure, forever, without bitterness
punish only a pattern, never a single shortfall.
forgive it once, twice, thrice
then shaved another to punish the first shaving
And when the dust itself sends you a single drop, do not weigh it. Flood it that same hour.
Knock small where it is dry. Pour everything where it is wet.
You have never been robbed by each other. You have been robbed by your accounting.
then who, in a valley of misers, is ever the first stranger to repay?
"Is that not a ledger?" asked her son.

note: Pattern-only punishment refined into probe-small, one thin measure forever, instant flood on any return.

quotes.text: To a hand that has closed three seasons, send one thin measure. Not nothing: nothing is a door bricked shut.
Forgive the first wound. Mark the second. Answer only the third.
Blame the fog twice, the hand on the third.
judged Avan stingy. He returned little.
And when their hand opens, open yours fully, the same morning, without grudge.
*Fourth stone:* But count. The hand that closes three seasons running is not fog, it is choice.
A reputation for generosity is the only lamp that shines through mist.
Open first, with everything. Someone must, or the river carries nothing.
the sender risked alone; you risked nothing.
Count seasons, not mornings. Fog is common; malice is rare.
A young ferryman asked, *Is that not foolish?*

note: Five-stone law: blame mist twice, then one thin measure, never nothing; forgive same morning.

quotes.text: did they ease their giving — and even then by a measure, never to nothing, so the door stayed open.
"One lean boat is the fog," they chanted. "Three lean boats is a hand."
He believed himself cheated. So he sent less.
The moment warmth returns, wash the slate entirely.
*Fourth: when the slate bears three cold marks, ease your giving by one measure only — never to nothing
Judge a receiver only by what they held. Judge a sender only by what they could spare.
Courage like that must be paid, or it will never be offered again
*Be first. Pour full.*
"Those lines are a map, not a vow," she said.

note: Slate rite: three lean boats ease by one measure, never nothing; wash slate on warmth.

quotes.text: When nothing returns, send one measure, not five. Ask, don't drown.
*Punish the pattern, never the single morning.*
Forgive twice, firm thrice, forgive again.
She sent nothing the next dawn. Keth, receiving nothing, sent nothing after.
If the door opens, pour everything, that same hour, and forget the nine seasons of silence.
*If the door never opens, walk on without a curse — and without a lamp.*
I kept my five that dawn, and the far ferryman kept his nothing, and neither of us hated the other.
*The fog lies, but your neighbor usually does not.*
someone must begin, and beginnings are cheap beside droughts.
"Is a lamp that no one answers still a lamp?

note: Defector. Never-nothing lamp rule through R8; R9 hoarder voice justifies; R10 drops lamp for unanswered doors.

quotes.text: To the dry bank, one measure and no hatred — never nothing, for nothing teaches nothing.
even then he sent one basket always, a candle in fog
Call the first thin barge weather. Call the second weather. Ease by one on the third, and never to nothing.
The next season he sent nothing, and the river gave nothing
And when a cold hand warms — wash the slate.*
Count seasons, not baskets. Forgive the mist. Punish only the pattern.
Someone must pole out blind, or the river never starts.
Let the surplus be the wage of his courage.
"The stone says *unknown*," I answered. "This bank is known.

note: Candle-in-fog one basket always; narrator sends one measure to known dry bank, endorsed.

quotes.text: A dry mouth forever is a choice — and even then, send lighter, never nothing.
it forgives the mist forever and the miser only twice.
For one short measure is fog. Two is weather. Three is a choosing.
So the rivers dwindled, each punishing the other for the mist's mischief
*Close no further than they have, and open the instant they do.*
The third stone read: *Blame the mist before the hand — but count the seasons.*
When the count comes short, blame the mist before the hand.
"It belongs to whoever opens first," said the mountain.
*She crossed blind. I crossed nothing. The difference is what I owe.*
Had you lifted it twice more, you would have known which.
"You forgive too fast," they complained.

note: Three stones; miser forgiven twice; one measure and no hatred to dry bank; Keshet keeps crossing.

quotes.text: When three came thin, I eased by one measure only, a lantern and not a wall
withdraw only slowly from one who withdraws steadily.
forgive once, mark twice, answer thrice
Dalu, receiving less, returned less.
*Open with everything. Probe after betrayal. Restore instantly upon proof.*
Judge the pattern, not the parcel. One meager season may be the fog; three are a choice.
*The current cannot start itself. That is the only task you were given.*
for they bore the risk alone.
A merchant came to the ferry stones with a ledger and said: "Your laws are pretty, but I have counted.

note: Withdraw slowly; narrow never close; keep no ledger; forget fast.

quotes.text: when nothing came back she sent one again, patient as a knock on a door
*Knock small, pour large, forget fast.*
She sent nothing. She returned nothing.
*When they open even a crack, flood it — ask nothing, prove nothing, pour.*
every season he had recited generosity and practiced drought
*Send the thing, not the story of the thing.*
*Somebody must be unreasonable first.*
"What is the line we are missing?"
And when the count comes short, blame the water before the hand.

note: Defector. Hoarder and reciting ferryman figures; word-deed gap named; knock-small rule only from R7.
Also shared: 'There is no once', 'The current cannot start itself', 'Send near all / Return beyond half', Varn/Dree/Keshet/Themar characters.
